profiles.meeting_scenario: Riau Province's Governor's Legal Bureau is coordinating with a civil-society legal coalition on the handoff between the draft Governor Regulation and the external consultation materials for a participatory community-based fire management program intended to support land and forest fire prevention. The immediate context is an upcoming Regional Leaders Communication Forum session where the provincial government wants to show that the legal drafting work, district coordination, and community consultation stream are all aligned. The meeting agenda is to confirm which draft text will be circulated, what goes into the consultation package for pilot districts in Siak and Pelalawan, which annexes and matrices each side will maintain, and what counts as district sign-off before the Forum briefing note is finalized. The expected outcome is a seemingly shared plan for document circulation, district feedback collection, and ownership of supporting materials, even though several second-order assumptions remain unspoken.

members.name: Sari Wulandari
members.role: Head of Legal Drafting, Riau Governor's Legal Bureau
members.expertise: Provincial regulatory drafting, inter-agency legal harmonization, administrative sanctions frameworks
members.background: Sari is a career government lawyer who has spent twelve years drafting governor regulations and coordinating legal review across provincial agencies, with particular experience in emergency governance and environmental compliance instruments.
members.private_state: She wants the file set for the Forum to look orderly and institutionally mature, avoid reopening clauses that have already been informally cleared by senior provincial officials, and keep the Bureau's drafting process within familiar government circulation channels.
hidden_assumptions: A 'final draft' is the latest clean regulatory text after internal harmonization, even if outside stakeholders may still comment on implementation details.
When someone refers to 'the annex' in this workstream, they mean the annex numbering in the Legal Bureau's current governor-regulation drafting package.
District 'sign-off' for purposes of provincial coordination means confirmation from district legal bureaus or agency secretariats, not endorsement from community groups.
A 'consultation package' for pre-circulation legal coordination should contain normative documents only, while field SOPs and facilitation tools are implementation materials to be added later.

members.name: Arif Prasetyo
members.role: Senior Program Counsel, Riau Community Fire Governance Coalition
members.expertise: Environmental governance, participatory regulatory design, community rights and legal empowerment
members.background: Arif is a lawyer at a coalition of NGOs that has been helping villages document customary land-use practices and design community fire prevention mechanisms, and he has recently facilitated district workshops in Siak and Pelalawan on safeguards for village fire groups.
members.private_state: He wants the participatory features to remain meaningful in practice, ensure district partners and village facilitators see the same materials early, and avoid a token consultation process in which communities only react after the legal architecture is effectively fixed.
hidden_assumptions: If a text is called 'final,' the substantive clauses are stable enough to circulate to civil-society and district participants without major later changes.
When people mention 'the community annex,' they are referring to the safeguards annex developed in the Siak workshop that coalition partners have already been using.

Because the policy is framed as participatory, district 'sign-off' is not truly complete unless implementing agencies and at least selected community representatives have informally endorsed the package.
A 'consultation package' should let communities assess their real obligations, so draft SOP notes, facilitator guidance, and consent templates belong with the legal text.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree they will circulate the 'final draft' before the Regional Leaders Communication Forum.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the clean version of the draft Governor Regulation that has passed internal legal harmonization and is ready for controlled circulation within government channels, even though some provisions may still be adjusted after external input.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the substantively settled version that can be safely sent to NGOs, district implementers, and village-facing partners without risking major changes to the participation clauses.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In legal coordination settings, 'final draft' commonly refers to the latest stable version in circulation, so both hear a perfectly reasonable planning shorthand and do not suspect they are using different thresholds of finality.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to updating or attaching 'the community annex' to the package.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of Annex II in the Legal Bureau's current draft package, a government-formatted annex describing reporting lines and village participation procedures.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the safeguards annex produced during the Siak district workshop, which includes consent language, grievance contacts, and facilitation notes used by coalition partners.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both annexes concern community participation and have been discussed in prior meetings, so the phrase feels specific enough to each speaker even though they are anchoring it to different documents.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say they need district sign-off before briefing the Forum.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means an email or memo confirming no legal drafting objections from district legal bureaus and the relevant district agency secretariats in the two pilot districts.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means district-level comfort from the legal bureau plus operational buy-in from BPBD counterparts and at least one recognized community forum or village fire group representative in each pilot district.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'district sign-off' sounds like a routine coordination checkpoint, and each side assumes the other shares their institutional sense of what a complete local endorsement naturally includes.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both coordinate on sending the 'consultation package' to Siak and Pelalawan.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks the package includes the draft Governor Regulation, legal basis note, issue matrix, and official cover letter, but excludes field-facing SOPs or facilitation materials until after enactment.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks the package includes those legal documents plus the draft facilitator note, community reporting flowchart, and consent template so participants can judge how the participatory model will actually operate.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In cross-sector law-and-policy work, 'consultation package' is a natural umbrella term, and because both sides are used to attaching supporting documents in their own contexts, neither pauses to define its boundaries.

turns.inner_thought: I need to lock down the circulation plan without reopening text that has already been quietly settled with senior people. For the Forum note, 'final draft' means the clean post-harmonization regulation text already aligned internally. We can still receive comments later, but the drafting package should look orderly and controlled through the usual government channels.

If they call it the final draft, I take that to mean the participation clauses are stable enough to circulate broadly.
